Reference: for each length, call task_func(length, seed). But task_func calls random.seed(seed) at each call! So each string uses the same seed — each string of the same length would be identical, and critically the RNG is reseeded each iteration. So the reference solution resets the seed per string, meaning the sequence starts fresh each time.

Solver: seeds once, then generates strings sequentially — the random stream continues across strings. So combined_frequency([10,20],0) with solver: first string = first 10 chars of stream; with reference: first string = first 10 chars, then reseed, second string = first 20 chars of same stream. Different results.

Hidden test expects reference behavior: expected output for [10,20] seed 0 shows 'y':2, 'W':3... wait check: reference re-seeds each iteration, so second string (length 20) = first 20 chars of seed-0 stream. First 10 chars: y W A c q G F z Y t (from f1(4) = first 4: y W A c). Expected dict: sum counts = 2+3+2+2+2+3+2+2+2+2+1+1+1+1+2+1+1 = 30 = 10+20. First string (10 chars) each char count 1; second string (20 chars) — overlapping chars get 1+count in second. 'y':2 means y appears once in each string — consistent with reseed. So the hidden test asserts reseed-per-string behavior (seed applied per call to task_func).

Solver's code: random.seed(seed) once, then loop. Solver verified [5] prefix matched, but [3,4,2] differs from reference. So the failure is a misapplication of the source pattern: task_func reseeds each call; solver's adaptation seeds once.
